consent_formula: S = 1 - prod(1 - w_i) over supportive items; O = 1 - prod(1 - w_i*m_i) over opposition items with m=1.0 (hard) or 0.6 (negotiable); consent_score = clamp(0.5 + 0.5*(S - O), 0, 1). Bands: >=0.65 GREEN-leaning, 0.35-0.65 AMBER, <0.35 RED-leaning; override: any hard item with weight>=0.8 and applies_to 'site' forces RED regardless of score. Weights are ASSUMED analyst judgments (each has a one-line rationale); this is a heuristic, not a validated model.
verdict_note: Consent layer only; says nothing about grid/physics. Weights are ASSUMED judgments.

items.weight_rationale: Same city, same utility, same year: a 50 MW project got administrative approval, 100+ speakers opposed, council delayed to Apr 2027 - this is the real consent test in Colorado Springs.
items.summary: Project Taurus (Raeden Corp, ~50 MW, former Intel plant, 1615 W Garden of the Gods Rd) was administratively approved; residents within 3 miles could appeal (Gazette Jun 16 fetched: confirms approval, 50 MW, appeal window; appeals later filed). Per search snippets: Planning Commission rejected appeals 6-2 on Jul 24 2026 with four conditions (>100 signed up against vs 13 for); Council voted 7-2 on Sep 17 2026 to delay the appeal decision to Apr 13 2027 so Raeden can negotiate a CSU large-load contract; Axios (Sep 22) says the developer is wavering. Not NOVVA, but shows the process any new CSU large load faces.

items.weight_rationale: Colorado Springs (NOVVA's jurisdiction, ASSUMED) has not adopted a moratorium while neighbors did; leadership quiet but permissive.
items.summary: 'Data Center moratoriums take hold along Front Range, but not Colorado Springs' (Alexander Edwards): Denver, Jefferson, Boulder, Larimer and Longmont adopted moratoriums/restrictions; Colorado Springs did not. 'City leadership in Colorado Springs has remained tight-lipped on Project Taurus.' Article does not explain why and does not mention NOVVA.

items.weight_rationale: First El Paso County municipality to pause (contagion risk to county-level action) but no unincorporated-county rule found.
items.summary: Monument Town Council approved a data-center moratorium (at least six months; no applications considered). No company had applied; proactive. Woodland Park (Teller Co.) passed an 18-month pause the week before (Gazette, search snippet). Article does not mention Colorado Springs.

items.weight_rationale: Denver 12-month, Jefferson Co. to Mar 2027 (1,500 ft setback), Larimer, Boulder: regional momentum, but Aurora rejected an indefinite pause.
items.summary: Denver Council Bill 26-0431: 12-month moratorium on new data-center permits (passed May 18 2026). Jefferson County moratorium extended to March 2027 with 1,500-ft setback from homes. Larimer and Boulder counties also paused. Aurora council voted down an indefinite moratorium (Colorado Politics, 2026-10-26). Details from search snippets only.

items.weight_rationale: Both 2026 bills died: no state incentive to sweeten a deal and no state regime, leaving decisions local.
items.summary: HB26-1030 (100% state sales/use tax exemption for qualifying data centers) failed 11-2 in House Energy & Environment and was postponed indefinitely; SB26-102 (Sen. Cathy Kipp, regulatory) was rewritten to include a tax incentive then postponed indefinitely at the sponsor's request. Search snippets only (Newsline fetch returned 403).

items.weight_rationale: Applies to any >10 MW customer: 10-year minimum contract and customer-paid infrastructure; a negotiable gate that governs expansion beyond today's load.
items.summary: Council (acting as utility board) gave final approval to a 2026 pricing plan with a Large Load Rate for new customers needing >10 MW; CSU says large customers sign a minimum 10-year agreement, pay for the infrastructure they need, and may qualify for incentives where they bring community value; CSU says it is the first Colorado utility with such a rate (csu.org blog 'Serving large data centers, protecting existing customers'). CPR page returned 403 and the CSU blog body was truncated: terms are from search summaries only. Whether NOVVA's existing load is grandfathered is NOT verified (ASSUMED yes for the existing 6 MW feed; any new >10 MW expansion ASSUMED covered).

items.weight_rationale: No NOVVA-specific opposition, petition or controversy found in ~40 search results; absence of evidence from a limited search.
items.summary: Searches for NOVVA + Colorado Springs returned only trade/real-estate coverage (2021 acquisition, expansion plans, Baxtel/DCD/JLL) and the Colorado Sun March 2024 piece; no petition, hearing or protest tied to NOVVA found. Local opposition centres on Project Taurus.

items.weight_rationale: Organized, well attended and able to file appeals; targeted at Taurus but builds a local anti-data-center constituency.
items.summary: Primary appeal filed by watchdog group Integrity Matters and Chelsea Glen residents (Colorado Politics); change.org petitions (an Apr 2026 petition demanding an immediate moratorium; another 'Reject the Project Taurus data center near Garden of the Gods'). The Sep 17 council meeting was described as raucous. Search snippets only.

items.weight_rationale: NOVVA's own claims (ambient/waterless cooling, PUE 1.3) answer the water objection raised in local threads; self-reported, unverified.
items.summary: Company page: ambient-air and waterless cooling, '8,000+ hours a year of ambient mountain air cooling', PUE 1.3 (annualized), chilled-water CRAH units. Self-reported.

items.weight_rationale: One 77-comment thread on Taurus: skeptical on water/noise/city motives, a couple supportive. Weak signal for NOVVA.
items.summary: 'Project Taurus/Data Center Community Meeting': 245 pts, 77 comments (11 captured). Top comments: drought/water worry, noise, distrust that the city weighs anything but revenue, power cost; a minority cite jobs / zoning fit.
